title: Review: Particles, isotopes and relative atomic mass; Mass spectrometry of elements; The mole and Avogadro constant; Ionic bonding and lattices; Periodic table structure and blocks; Balanced equations and reacting masses; Molar gas volume and Avogadro's law; Empirical and molecular formulae
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AM01#t2 term and clue written for the game; AM01#t3 term and clue written for the game; AS01#t1 term and clue written for the game; BD01#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM01#N.9, AM02#N.11, AM05#N.9, AM07#N.14, BD01#N.14a, AM05#N.10a, BD01#N.15.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Amount of substance
items.clue: The quantity with symbol n, found by dividing a mass by M.

items.label: Avogadro constant
items.clue: Multiply n by this value to get the number of particles, N.

items.label: Atomic number
items.clue: The count of protons in a nucleus, symbol Z, which fixes the element.

items.label: Cation
items.clue: A positively charged particle formed when a metal atom loses electrons.

questions.stem: A one-carat diamond is pure carbon with a mass of 0.200 g. About how many carbon atoms does it contain? Data: Ar C 12.0; N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
questions.explanation: n = 0.200 g ÷ the molar mass of C = 0.0167 mol. N = 0.0167 mol × N_A = 1.00 × 10²² atoms.

questions.stem: Ethyne, a welding gas, and benzene, a liquid, both contain 92.3% carbon and 7.7% hydrogen by mass. What is the molecular formula of benzene? Data: Ar H 1.0, C 12.0. Mr of benzene = 78.0.
questions.explanation: C: 92.3 ÷ 12 ≈ 7.7; H: 7.7 ÷ 1 ≈ 7.7. Ratio 1 : 1, empirical formula CH (about 13). x = 78 ÷ 13 = 6: C₆H₆.

questions.stem: In the molar gas volume experiment, a student uses magnesium ribbon with a thin oxide coating that has not been cleaned off. How does this affect the calculated molar gas volume?

options.text: It is too high, because the oxide reacts with the acid to make extra gas.
It is too low, because part of the mass weighed gives no hydrogen.
It is unchanged, because the acid is in excess and all the solid reacts.
It is too high, because the calculated amount of magnesium is too large.

questions.explanation: n(Mg) is calculated from the full mass, but some is MgO. Less H₂ forms than expected, so V ÷ n is too small.

questions.stem: A strip of magnesium burns brightly in air and leaves white magnesium oxide: 2Mg(s) + O₂(g) → 2MgO(s). What mass of MgO forms from 2.43 g of Mg? (Ar: O 16.0, Mg 24.3)
Ionic radii (pm): Na⁺ 102, K⁺ 138, F⁻ 133, Cl⁻ 181. Which shows the strength of the ionic bonding in NaF, NaCl and KCl in decreasing order?
questions.explanation: All are 1+ and 1−, so radii decide. Radius sums: NaF 235, NaCl 283, KCl 319 pm. Closer centres, stronger attraction.

questions.stem: Two identical flasks at the same temperature and pressure are filled, one with neon, Ne, and one with sulfur hexafluoride, SF₆, a dense gas used in electrical switchgear. The SF₆ flask holds 7.2 times the mass of gas. Which statement is correct? (Ar: F 19.0, Ne 20.2, S 32.1)

options.text: The SF₆ flask holds 7.2 times as many particles as the neon flask.
The neon flask holds more particles, because neon atoms are much smaller.
Both flasks hold the same number of particles; each SF₆ molecule is about 7.2 times heavier.
Both flasks hold the same number of atoms, so there are 7 times as many Ne atoms as SF₆ molecules.

questions.explanation: Avogadro's law: same V, T and p → same number of particles. 146.1 ÷ 20.2 = 7.2.

questions.stem: In a kettle's heating element, the hot metal wire is packed in powdered magnesium oxide, MgO, inside a metal tube. MgO is ionic, yet it is used here as an electrical insulator. Why doesn't it conduct?

options.text: MgO contains no ions until it is dissolved or melted.
Its ions are held in fixed positions, and MgO stays solid at the element's temperature.
Its electrons are all shared in covalent bonds, so none are free to move.
Its ions are too highly charged to move, even when MgO is molten.

questions.explanation: Charge flows only if charged particles can move. In the solid the ions are locked in the lattice and there are no free electrons. Strong 2+/2− attractions keep MgO solid to about 2850 °C.
